g2-P2P3b:
The usual argument is monogamy versus free love, and that starts one level too late. My Romance Guide has the longer version. Here I'll just say the community problem plainly: living in close quarters makes jealousy bigger, and jealousy can capture either system.

Rigid monogamy can turn fear and possession into a moral law. With free love, if there's no inner pl/ork, the same fear can just get spread over a bigger spreadsheet. And whatever label you put on a relationship, it won't release childhood panic. It won't release comparison or abandonment terror either, or the wish to control another person.
g2-P4P5:
I don't think a community should choose the form for everyone. Couples can make different agreements, and so can people in other relationship configurations. They can revise those agreements, too. And when the agreements bring up old material, they can ask for support.

Whatever forms people choose, their housing shouldn't depend on staying inside one romantic agreement. Neither should their children's security, or their membership, or their access to common necessities.
